title: Recovering a bad coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ coordinates. A coordinate restriction $\rho$ is bad when the restricted Boolean function is nonconstant. For every such bad restriction, extend it by fixing its selected bad coordinate to the sign chosen by the formula's construction; changing that coordinate back to free recovers $\rho$ exactly.
hypotheses_covered: The formula is a DNF on $n$ coordinates
The input restriction is bad, meaning its restricted Boolean function is nonconstant
